stem: The cartoon shows the embargo biting an American merchant, not a British or French one. Which of the following best explains the embargo's most important unintended effect?

options.text: It forced Britain and France to stop seizing American ships on the seas at once.
options.misconception: Britain and France kept seizing ships; the embargo hurt American trade far more than theirs.

options.text: It made American farmers rich by raising the price of cotton in Europe.
options.misconception: The embargo cut off exports, so farm prices fell and farmers suffered, not grew rich.

options.text: It ended all trade between the North and the South for a full decade.
options.misconception: Trade between the regions continued; the embargo blocked foreign trade, not trade at home.

options.text: It cut Americans off from British goods, so Americans began making those goods at home.

rationales.A: Britain and France kept seizing ships. The embargo hurt American trade far more than theirs.
rationales.B: The embargo cut off exports, so farm prices fell and farmers suffered, not grew rich.
rationales.C: Trade between the regions continued. The embargo blocked foreign trade, not trade at home.
rationales.D: With British cloth and iron cut off, Americans had to supply themselves. Background: new mills and workshops opened, and the embargo became an accidental push toward American manufacturing.
rationales.general:
1. Start with the plan. Stop all foreign trade, and Britain and France will feel the pain.
2. Ask who felt it instead. American merchants and farmers, whose goods sat unsold in port.
3. Ask what changed at home. With no British goods to buy, Americans built mills and shops to make their own.
4. Put it together. A policy meant to punish Europe ended up building American industry.
Remember: a ban on imports can become a gift to home factories, even when nobody planned it.
